scenarios.title: Default format: the list command gives the slice's attempt branches and the prompt's steps delete them
scenarios.notes: Scratch repo, default format. Branches sdlc/S-001-attempt-1, -attempt-2, sdlc/S-001, sdlc/S-001-v0. Run the exact command text from integrator.md Clean up step 2. Only the two attempt branches must come back, in order. After the local delete, git branch --list shows the other two.

scenarios.title: Custom lowercase format: the id comes back as s-001 and the case-blind filter still keeps it
scenarios.notes: branchFormat feature/PROJ-1-{name:lower}. The list prints id s-001. A filter on S-001 with case kept finds nothing, so the filter must ignore case. Try also a mixed-case format and a slice id such as S-027b with a letter suffix. Check S-001 does not match S-0010 or S-001a.

scenarios.title: Attempt branches of other slices and non-attempt branches stay
scenarios.notes: Branches of S-002, S-0010, S-001a, the run branch, verify branches and the user's own branches must survive. Branch names with odd characters (dash-leading, slash, unicode, spaces) must not break quoting or flags in git branch -D and git push --delete. Use attack-corpus names.

scenarios.title: pr, mr and stack modes delete each attempt branch on origin; a missing remote ref is fine
scenarios.notes: Scratch repo with a bare origin. Push attempt-1 only, keep attempt-2 local. Run the prompt's local delete and git push origin --delete for each. The pushed ref must vanish. The missing ref must not stop the run. In direct mode no push happens (read the prompt text for the mode list).

scenarios.title: Parent walk: a finished rejected parent gets the same list-and-delete, an unfinished parent keeps its branches
scenarios.notes: S-013 split into S-013a and S-013b. Check the text uses step 2 per parent id, keeps the splitInto rule and the never-delete-unfinished sentence. Run the list for the parent id under a custom format.

scenarios.title: Prompt text: no literal attempt pattern remains in Clean up, and the text passes the STE check
scenarios.notes: integrator.md Clean up holds no sdlc/<id>-attempt and no -attempt-*. The sdlc/<id>-v* half in step 1 stays for S-027c. ste-check.py passes. Step 1 now points to step 2 for attempts.

tools.purpose: Run branches.py list and git commands from scratch repos with a bare origin
Hostile branch names for the delete commands

riskReason: One prompt changes, but a wrong list filter leaves dead branches or deletes a live one in a user's repo.
notes: Prompt-only slice. No endpoint, UI or async path, so cli, contract and security cover it. Limits is not tagged because the spec states no number. Verifiers run the prompt's exact commands against scratch git repos.
